ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A parasite before treatment

A 38-year-old man is being evaluated for mepolizumab because of severe eosinophilic asthma. His workup also identifies an active helminth infection. What is the most appropriate approach to this infection before starting the biologic?

  1. Treat the existing helminth infection before initiating mepolizumab
  2. Start mepolizumab to eradicate the helminth directly
  3. Ignore the infection because eosinophils are always harmful
  4. Treat only after a first biologic dose causes symptoms
  5. Use omalizumab as an antiparasitic substitute
Answer and explanation

Treat the existing helminth infection before initiating mepolizumab

Eosinophils participate in host responses to some parasites; the label advises treating pre-existing helminth infection.

Option explanations

Treat the existing helminth infection before initiating mepolizumab: Eosinophils participate in host responses to some parasites; the label advises treating pre-existing helminth infection.

Start mepolizumab to eradicate the helminth directly: Mepolizumab is not an antiparasitic drug.

Ignore the infection because eosinophils are always harmful: Eosinophils have host-defense roles as well as disease-related effects.

Treat only after a first biologic dose causes symptoms: Known infection should be addressed before initiation.

Use omalizumab as an antiparasitic substitute: Omalizumab is not a treatment for helminth infection.
